questions.text: Indicate the syllable that bears the stress in the following words: (i) IN-SAN-I-TY (ii) CEL-I-BRA-TION (iii) LIT-E-RA-TURE (iv) DOC-TOR (v) CON-TEMP-TI-BLE (vi) TES-TI-MO-NY (vii) DE-PART-MENT (viii) PO-LY-SY-LLAB-IC

Identify the sound underlined in each of the following words by writing out its phonemic symbol (e.g. late /eɪ/): perpetual, English, knowledge, handsome, thorough, cheer, knowledge, rude. (4 marks) (The paper underlines one sound in each word; the underlining is not reproduced here.)

Read the extract: 'Maxim Boanno was the son of an immigrant Italian construction worker and a local Fezzanni woman. And he took his order from your father. After Independence, your father lost grip of the situation in Fezzan because the black guys who took over the reins of government hated his guts. They felt he should be removed from the scene...' (i) Who is the speaker? (ii) Who is being addressed? (iii) What is the name of the father in question? (iv) What does the phrase 'to be removed from the scene' mean? (v) The figure of speech used in the last sentence of the extract is ____. (2.5 marks)
In a length not exceeding the space provided, comment on the subject/theme of violence in Emmanuel Omobowale's Seasons of Rage. (2 marks)

Read the extract: 'There goes the list again. Are you not the one that used to tell us that Taiwo's destiny is not the same as Kehinde's? I am seriously thinking about it.... My problem is my job, it is too demanding.' (i) Who is the speaker? (ii) Who is spoken to? (iii) What is the subject of discussion? (iv) What job is referred to in the last sentence of the extract? (v) How would you categorise the italicised expression (Taiwo's destiny is not the same as Kehinde's): proverb, idiom or axiom? (2.5 marks)
In a length not exceeding the space provided, discuss Adenike Akinjobi's Mirage as a play built on the principle of poetic justice. (2 marks)

Read the extract: 'Your absence is like a / heavy blow on my back, / as herdsman hits the nearest cow, / so is life without you! / Like tea without sugar, / so is life without you, / Like a bat beaten up by rain,' (i) Identify the dominant figure of speech in the extract. (ii) What is the mood of the poetic persona here? (iii) Lines 3 and 7 of the extract make use of which kind of imagery? (iv) What is the subject matter of the extract/poem? (2 marks)
In a length not exceeding the space provided, discuss the title-poem in Bisi Oyerele's collection as an elegy. (2 marks)
In about 250 words, write an article on the on-going controversy about President Muhammadu Buhari's health and what should be done.

Indicate the syllable that bears the stress in the following words: (i) IN-SE-CU-RI-TY (ii) COR-O-NA-TION (iii) MAG-NIF-I-CENT (iv) TEA-CHER (v) CON-TRIB-U-TORY (vi) TES-TI-MO-NI-AL (vii) LEG-I-SLA-TIVE (viii) UN-PRE-DIC-TA-BLE (4 marks)

Identify the sound underlined in each of the following words by writing out its phonemic symbol (e.g. late /eɪ/): faithful, nurse, boys, quay, chauffeur, browse, knight, lower. (4 marks) (The paper underlines one sound in each word; the underlining is not reproduced here.)

Read the extract: 'You asked for Mr Boanno's protection. This means that you both have to play the game according to his rules. I don't know what this Pendelton man has done that necessitated the destruction of one of his supermarkets and I don't care.' (i) Who is the speaker? (ii) 'You' in the first sentence above refers to ____ and ____. (iii) Where is the speech made? (iv) Besides the addressee, who else is present here? (v) What is the last serious action performed by the speaker? (6 marks)
In a length not exceeding the space provided, discuss Martin as a villain in Emmanuel Omobowale's Seasons of Rage. (4 marks)

Read the extract: 'When we had you, many people, especially our enemies, thought you would go like others. Some rejoiced with us and went behind us to say terrible things.' (i) Who is the speaker? (ii) Who is spoken to? (iii) What is the initial subject of discussion between the speaker and the addressee? (iv) What is the latter subject of discussion between the speaker and the addressee? (5 marks)
In a length not exceeding the space provided, discuss Remi as the protagonist in Adenike Akinjobi's Mirage. (4 marks)

Read the extract: 'The owner of 'Ire', / I invoke you, / appear, / like a thunderbolt. / With a thunder clap, / thunderously descend / on my enemies, / match on them, / crumble them, / pulverize them, / and let their remains, / remain floating on river,' (i) What is the mood of the poetic persona here? (ii) Lines 3 and 4 illustrate which figure of speech? (iii) What is the subject matter of the extract/poem? (iv) The extract is taken from a poem entitled ____. (4 marks)
In a length not exceeding the space provided, discuss the poem entitled 'Ogbomoso' in Bisi Oyerele's collection. (4 marks)
In about 250 words, write an essay on the perennial problem of fuel scarcity in the country.
